section: M.M. Punchhi Commission (2007) - recommendations and their status
subsections: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: The report of the M.M. Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was submitted in which year and in how many volumes?
o: 2010 in seven volumes
2015 in eight volumes
2007 in five volumes
2012 in six volumes
accepted.x: The Punchhi Commission report was submitted in 2010 and comprised seven volumes.
accepted.tq: Use the paired year-and-number recall method for closely related quantitative facts.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: The report of the M.M. Punchhi Commission was referred to which body for consideration?
o: National Development Council
Inter-State Council
Finance Commission
Zonal Council
accepted.x: The report was referred to the Inter-State Council for consideration.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional or intergovernmental body associated with the subject.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: With reference to the present status of the major recommendations of the M.M. Punchhi Commission, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The major recommendations have not been implemented, though the report was considered by the Inter-State Council.
All major recommendations have been fully implemented by the Union Government.
The recommendations were implemented only through constitutional amendments.
The report was rejected before being referred to the Inter-State Council.
accepted.x: The major recommendations of the Punchhi Commission have not been implemented, although the report was referred to and considered by the Inter-State Council.
accepted.tq: Distinguish consideration of a commission report from actual implementation of its recommendations.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: Article 156 of the Constitution continues to provide that a Governor shall hold office:
o: during the pleasure of the President
during the pleasure of the Chief Minister of the State
for a fixed term of six years irrespective of the Union Government
until removed by the State Legislature
accepted.x: Article 156 continues to provide that the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
accepted.tq: Apply the article-number and authority pairing without swapping the constitutional authority.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an aspect of the continuing position concerning State Governors?
o: Governors are appointed by the Inter-State Council and act only as ceremonial heads.
Governors continue to hold office during the pleasure of the President and continue to act as Chancellors.
Governors hold office during the pleasure of the State Legislature but cannot act as Chancellors.
Governors no longer hold office during the pleasure of the President and cannot act as Chancellors.
accepted.x: Since Article 156 remains unchanged, Governors continue to hold office during the pleasure of the President. They also continue to act as Chancellors.
accepted.tq: Separate the two continuing features instead of accepting a partially correct statement.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s:
Arrange the following judicial developments concerning gubernatorial action on Bills in chronological order:
A. Presidential Reference opinion holding that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent
B. Judgment in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor
C. Judgment in State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu
o: B, C, A
C, B, A
B, A, C
A, B, C
accepted.x: The chronological order is B (2023), C (8 April 2025), and A (20 November 2025).
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the known 2023 judgment and then place the two 2025 developments.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the later judicial developments concerning timelines for gubernatorial action on Bills?
o: The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case fixed timelines, whereas the 20 November 2025 Presidential Reference held that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
The 2023 Punjab case fixed binding timelines, while the 2025 Presidential Reference abolished all judicial review.
The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case held that Governors may indefinitely withhold assent, and the Presidential Reference confirmed it.
Both the 2023 Punjab case and the 2025 Presidential Reference held that deemed assent is mandatory.
accepted.x: The Tamil Nadu case of 8 April 2025 fixed timelines, but the Presidential Reference opinion of 20 November 2025 held that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely dated judgments by matching each ruling with its exact legal consequence.
accepted.sec: Status - report volumes and Centre's acceptance

accepted.s: The Union Finance Minister stated that cesses and surcharges are levied for specific purposes and are outside the divisible pool. In 2025–26, the divisible pool was stated to be approximately what proportion of gross tax revenue?
o: 61 percent
71 percent
81 percent
91 percent
accepted.x: The divisible pool was stated to be about 81 percent of gross tax revenue in 2025–26. Cesses and surcharges, being levied for specific purposes, remain outside it.
accepted.tq: Link the fiscal concept with its stated percentage while avoiding reversed-share options.

accepted.s: The issue of cesses and surcharges being kept outside the divisible pool is significant in relation to the Punchhi Commission because:
o: it determines the appointment of State Governors
it concerns the same question of the distribution of fiscal resources between the Union and the States
it governs the tenure of the Inter-State Council
it relates exclusively to the reorganisation of States
accepted.x: The treatment of cesses and surcharges affects the distribution of fiscal resources between the Union and the States, which is the same federal-finance issue raised by the Punchhi Commission.
accepted.tq: Apply the underlying federal principle to a contemporary fiscal situation.

accepted.s: Which of the following States is specifically included among the southern States whose share was raised under the revised formula of the 16th Finance Commission?
o: Haryana
Punjab
Andhra Pradesh
Rajasthan
accepted.x: The revised formula raised the share of the five southern States, including Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the relevant State from the regional comparison rather than from unrelated State options.

accepted.s: The Centre for Devolution and Inclusive Federalism (CDI) considers which combination of measures as a route back to cooperative federalism?
o: Bill deadlines, a mandatory Inter-State Council and a cap on cesses
Governor elections, abolition of the Finance Commission and a single tax rate
State emergency powers, abolition of surcharges and direct election of Governors
Abolition of the Inter-State Council, longer Bill pendency and unrestricted cesses
accepted.x: The CDI identifies bill deadlines, a mandatory Inter-State Council and a cap on cesses as the Punchhi agenda capable of contributing to cooperative federalism.
accepted.tq: Group the three associated agenda items and reject options containing reversed or contrary measures.
